hints: Remember an ester is made from a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol, so focus on what the alcohol part must be if the acid is fixed as methanoic acid.
Methanoate is $\text{HCOO-}$, which uses 1 carbon, so the alcohol alkyl group must supply the other 4 carbons as a $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ group. List the four different butyl structures.
Check each butyl methanoate for a chiral centre, then add one extra isomer for any structure that can exist as a pair of enantiomers to get the total count.
walkthrough:
**Work out the alcohol fragment**

Think of ester formation simply as acid + alcohol. Here the acid is fixed.

$$\text{HCOOH} + \text{ROH} \rightarrow \text{HCOOR} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the formula of R**

The product must be $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$. The methanoate part, $\text{HCOO}$, already gives $\text{C}_1\text{H}_1\text{O}_2$.

So R must be $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$. We need all butyl methanoates, $\text{HCOOC}_4\text{H}_9$.

**Draw the four structural butyl groups**

There are four ways to arrange $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ as an alcohol residue. Lovely and systematic if you list them.

1. $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (n-butyl)
2. $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ (2-methylpropyl, isobutyl)
3. $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ (tert-butyl)
4. $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (sec-butyl)

**Check for stereoisomerism**

Look for a carbon with four different groups. Only the sec-butyl ester has this.

$$\text{HCOO-CH}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)$$ 
The starred carbon is bonded to H, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{OCOH}$, so it is chiral and exists as two enantiomers.

**Add up the total**

Count 1 each for n-butyl, isobutyl and tert-butyl, plus 2 for sec-butyl.

$$1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 5 \text{ isomeric esters}$$

options.A: 2 is far too low. It misses most of the butyl structural isomers and ignores stereoisomerism completely.
options.B: 3 is too low. You might get this if you only think of n-butyl, isobutyl and tert-butyl, forgetting the sec-butyl structure and its chirality.
options.C: 4 counts the four structural butyl groups correctly but misses the key trap. The sec-butyl ester is chiral, so it adds one extra stereoisomer.
options.D: 5 is correct: n-butyl methanoate, isobutyl methanoate, tert-butyl methanoate (3 isomers) plus two enantiomers of sec-butyl methanoate (2 isomers) gives 5 in total.
